Our mission is to create a community where mathematics is not just about formulas but about critical thinking, curiosity, and teamwork. This club allows students to go beyond textbooks and experience the true beauty of numbers and logic.

Whether it's competitions, workshops, or friendly discussions, we want every member to feel inspired and motivated to see math not as pressure, but as passion.

testimonials.message: As General Secretary, my role is to keep our Math Club organized, active, and welcoming for everyone. I work to ensure smooth coordination of events, competitions, and activities so that each member has the chance to participate and grow. Together, we are creating a community where learning mathematics is not only meaningful but also enjoyable.

testimonials.name: Monwar Rafat

We aim to make mathematics a source of joy, exploration, and innovation for every student, giving them opportunities to learn and lead with confidence.

testimonials.name: Arefin Anwar
testimonials.message: As Vice President, I believe the true strength of our Math Club lies in teamwork and inclusiveness. We are building a community where students not only sharpen their problem-solving skills but also learn to innovate, collaborate, and enjoy mathematics as a lifelong journey of discovery.

events.title: BEYOND NUMBERS
Math Olympiad
events.description:
The Math Olympiad is a competitive platform designed to inspire young minds and
celebrate the beauty of mathematics. Participants will showcase their problem-solving skills across four categories:
* Primary (Class 3–5)
* Junior (Class 6–8)
* Secondary (Class 9–10)
* Higher Secondary (Class 11–12 and HSC 2025–HSC 2027)

The contest duration is 1 Hour and will consist of 8–12 challenging find based problems, carefully selected to assess creativity, logical reasoning, and mathematical depth. The questions will cover core areas of mathematics, including:
* Number Theory
* Algebra
* Geometry
* Combinatorics
The level of difficulty will be equivalent to the BdMO Regional Round, ensuring fairness and rigor for each category. This event aims to encourage analytical thinking and foster a deeper appreciation of problem-solving among students at different academic Stages.

events.title: IQ Test
events.description:
IQ Test is a challenging and engaging event open to participants across all four categories:
* Primary (Class 3–5)
* Junior (Class 6–8)
* Secondary (Class 9–10)
* Higher Secondary (Class 11–12 and HSC 2025–HSC 2027)
Objective:
Participants will attempt 20 brainteasers designed to test logical reasoning, analyt-
ical thinking, and problem-solving ability. Each question requires careful thought and a high level of IQ to arrive at the correct solution.
Event Structure:
* The event will last for 30 minutes or more, depending on the difficulty .
* All participants must work individually and rely solely on their own reasoning and Scoring and Winners
* Correct answers will be awarded points according to difficulty.
* The top three participants from each category will be rewarded.
* Any attempt to tamper with another participant’s work or use unauthorized aids may result in disqualification.
This event emphasizes cognitive skills, quick thinking, and analytical reasoning, providing a fun yet challenging platform for participants to showcase their intelligence.

events.title: Probability Pressure
events.description:
Probability Pressure is a focused problem-solving event for participants in the Secondary (Class 9–10) and Higher Secondary (Class 11–12 and HSC 2025–HSC
2027) categories.
Event Structure :
* Participants will be given a set of 7–8 probability-based questions.
* The problems may involve applications of geometry, number theory, and related
mathematical fields.
* The event will last for 45 minutes, during which participants must attempt to solve
all questions.
Scoring and Winners :
* Participants who provide a flawless solution will be awarded full marks.
* Partial marks may be awarded for rough work or incomplete solutions that demon-
strate clear reasoning.
* The top three participants from each category will be rewarded.
* Any attempt to tamper with another participant’s work or use unauthorized aids may result in disqualification.
This event emphasizes logical reasoning, probabilistic thinking, and accuracy,
encouraging participants to carefully analyze and solve problems within the given time.

events.title: Human Calculator
events.description:
The Human Calculator challenge is a thrilling test of mental arithmetic and numerical
agility designed for students across all categories. Participants will compete in a written round where they must solve a series of complex calculations using only their minds, with
Objective:
Participants must accurately solve a set of mathematical problems under a strict time
limit. The questions will test speed and precision in various areas of mental calculation, including but not limited to addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, percentages, squares, and roots. The individual who correctly solves the most problems within the
allotted time will be crowned the ”Human Calculator.”
Rules :
* The event is open to participants from Primary (Class 3–5), Junior (Class 6–8),
Secondary (Class 9–10), and Higher Secondary (Class 11–12) categories.
* Each participant will receive a question paper and an answer sheet. Scratch paper
will be provided for working out calculations.
* The use of calculators, electronic devices, or any pre-written formulas is strictly
prohibited. All calculations must be performed by the participant.
* All working must be shown on the provided scratch paper. The question paper
must not be used for rough work.
* All final answers must be clearly written on the provided answer sheet.
* The event will be a 60-minute written round.
* Winners will be determined based on the highest number of correct answers. In
case of a tie, the participant who finished in the shortest time will be awarded the
higher position.
* Top performers from each category will receive awards and recognition.
* Any attempt to use unauthorized aids or communicate with another participant
will result in immediate disqualification.
This event challenges concentration, memory, and rapid problem-solving skills, celebrating the incredible power of the human mind as the ultimate computational toolsection

events.title: Calculus Bee
events.description:
This competition will focus exclusively on calculus problems. Participants will be challenged with questions from both Differentiation and Integration, covering key concepts and techniques from each area. From finding derivatives of functions to solving integrals, you'll need to apply your calculus knowledge to solve these problems accurately. This will test both problem-solving speed and precision of each participant.

CATEGORIES: Secondary and Higher Secondary 
DURATION: 45 MIN
FORMAT: SOLO

RULES:
1. No External Aids
All calculations must be done by hand; calculators, phones, or any other aids are strictly prohibited.

2. Zero Tolerance for Unfair Means
Any form of cheating or collusion will result in immediate disqualification.

3. Merit Depends on Process
Merit is awarded for a clear, step-by-step solution—even if the final answer is incorrect, a sound method earns partial credit.

4. Winner Selection
a. Contestants will have to solve the problems which will be given from both differentiation and integration.
b. There will be three winners from each category. Winners will be awarded.

events.title: Geometry Dash
events.description:
Geometry Dash is a thrilling problem-solving contest crafted exclusively for the Sec-
ondary (Class 9–10) and Higher Secondary (Class 11–12 and HSC 2025–HSC
2027) categories. This event is dedicated to exploring the elegance, depth, and challenge
of geometry.
Event Structure
* The contest will feature 5–7 “find-based/proof-based” geometry problems,
designed to test conceptual understanding, logical reasoning, and creative applica-
tion.
* Each problem requires participants to derive, prove, or find specific values, relations,
or constructions through mathematical reasoning.
* The total duration of the event will be 45 minutes.
Evaluation
* A flawless solution will be awarded full marks.
* Partial credit will be given for substantial progress, rough work, or correct approaches even if the final solution is not reached.
* Any kind of unfair means will lead to immediate disqualification.
Winners:
* The top three participants from each category (Secondary and Higher Secondary) will be declared winners.
This event emphasizes the beauty and power of geometry, encouraging participants to appreciate both precision and creativity in mathematical problem-solving.

events.title: Rubik's Cube
events.description:
The Rubik’s Cube Showdown is an exciting test of speed, focus, and problem-solving skills, where participants will battle it out to prove their cubing mastery. The event will be divided into two rounds, combining both individual performance and head-to-head competition.

Categories :

* Primary (Class 3–5)
* Junior (Class 6–8)
* Secondary (Class 9–10)
* Higher Secondary (Class 11–12 and HSC 2025–HSC 2027)

Event Structure:

Round 1 – Preliminary (Speed Round):

All registered participants will attempt to solve the Rubik’s Cube.

Each participant will be given multiple solves (depending on time constraints), and their best time will be recorded.

Based on performance, the top 6 participants with the fastest solving times will advance to the final round.

Round 2 – Final (1v1 Knockout Matches):

The four finalists will compete in 1v1 head-to-head matches.

Pairings will be made based on seeding from Round 1 (fastest vs. slowest, etc.).

In each match, both participants will solve the same scrambled cube simultaneously.

The winner will be the participant who completes the solve first.

Matches continue until a final champion is determined.

Winners:

Champion – Winner of the final duel.

First Runner-Up – The finalist defeated in the championship match.

Second Runner-Up – Determined from the duel between the semi-final losers

events.title: Sudoku
events.description:
The Sudoku Challenge is an engaging puzzle competition designed to test participants’
logical reasoning, pattern recognition, and problem-solving speed. Participants will solve
Sudoku grids of varying difficulty within a limited time, aiming to fill each grid correctly
according to the classic rules of Sudoku.
Categories :
The competition is open for the following four categories:
* Primary (Class 3–5)
* Junior (Class 6–8)
* Secondary (Class 9–10)
* Higher Secondary (Class 11–12 and HSC 2025–HSC 2027) Rules of Sudoku
* Each Sudoku puzzle consists of a 9×9 grid, divided into nine 3×3 subgrids (also called
boxes or regions).
* The goal is to fill the empty cells with numbers from 1 to 9.
* Each row, each column, and each 3.3 subgrid must contain all numbers from 1 to
9 exactly once.
* Participants cannot repeat any number in a row, column, or subgrid.
* The time taken to complete the puzzle will be considered in determining the
winners.
* Time duration of this event will be 30 minutes.
* The three fastest participants in each category who complete the puzzle correctly
will be declared the winners. Three winners from each category .
* Any incorrect entries or attempts to alter another participant’s puzzle may
result in disqualification.
This event encourages focus, logical reasoning, and careful planning, offering a fun and competitive way to strengthen numerical and analytical skills.

events.title: Cryptomania
events.description:
Cryptomania is an exciting solo event open to participants across all four categories:
* Primary (Class 3–5)
* Junior (Class 6–8)
* Secondary (Class 9–10)
* Higher Secondary (Class 11–12 and HSC 2025–HSC 2027)
Objective :
Participants will solve cipher-decipher challenges or thrilling problem-based cases
using logical reasoning and analytical skills. A cipher is a method of transforming
information to keep it secret, while deciphering is the process of decoding it to reveal the
original message. Participants must extract clues and reason carefully to solve the tasks.
Rules
* Each participant must solve the problems using sheer problem-solving skills; ex-
ternal aids are not allowed.
* Participants will be provided all necessary information within the problem state
* there will be three winners from each category.
* Any attempt to tamper with another participant’s work or use unauthorized aids may result in disqualification.
This event encourages critical thinking, creativity, and logical deduction, offering participants a fun and challenging opportunity to crack codes and solve mysteries.

articles.title: Trivuj_Choturdoshi_(3rd-part)
articles.author: Maaz Deen Sanjid Kabir
articles.content:
And just like that, we have reached the final destination of our geometric journey. Today marks the release of the third and final volume of the "Triangle Fourteenth" (Trivuj Choturdoshi) series, where all the foundational pieces we built earlier come together in perfect harmony.

This grand finale is an exploration of high-level, awe-inspiring theorems. We will witness how Napoleon’s Theorem unravels a hidden equilateral triangle from the chaos of any ordinary shape, how Desargues’ Theorem expands our vision into three-dimensional projective thinking, and how a magical Nine-Point Circle naturally emerges from a basic triangle. To complete the masterpiece, we also dive into the intricate structures of Orthic Triangles, Medial Triangles, Euler Lines, and Pedal Triangles.

This final part is the culmination of our geometric saga, passionately put together by our academic member, Maaz Deen Sanjid Kabir.

articles.title: Trivuj_Choturdoshi_(2nd-part)
articles.author: Maaz Deen Sanjid Kabir
articles.content:
After establishing some powerful foundational theorems in our first part, we are back with the second volume of our series, "Triangle Fourteenth" (Trivuj Choturdoshi). This time, we are stepping deeper into a mesmerizing world of circles, angles, and symmetry.

This second part explores theorems that elevate geometric beauty to a whole new level. We look at the harmony of Incircles and Excircles as they perfectly embrace the boundaries of a triangle, and the Steiner–Lehmus Theorem, which reveals a fascinating symmetry within angle bisectors. Furthermore, we unpack Menelaus's Theorem to unlock the secrets of collinear points, and the sheer magic of Morley’s Trisector Theorem, which divides angles to reveal a hidden equilateral triangle inside any given triangle.

This volume is a continuous journey into the symmetry and structure of advanced geometry, brought to you by our academic member, Maaz Deen Sanjid Kabir.
articles.excerpt: A short description of the article...

articles.title: Trivuj_Choturdoshi_(1st-part)
articles.author: Maaz Deen Sanjid Kabir
articles.content:
Behind the hidden lines and equations of everyday geometry lies a world of pure elegance. What first appears to be a tangled web of lines and angles often unfolds into something beautifully simple once you apply the right principles.

Today, we are excited to share the first part of our geometric series, "Triangle Fourteenth" (Trivuj Choturdoshi). This part is a journey beyond standard textbook problems into the heart of advanced geometric thinking.

In this first volume, we dive deep into the Extended Law of Sines, discovering how it forms a perfect bridge between a triangle and its circumcircle. We also explore the sheer elegance of Ceva's and Intersection theorems—proving the flawless confluence of concurrent lines—alongside a beautiful breakdown of area ratios through Routh's Theorem.

This article is a small exploration of the foundational elegance hidden inside triangle geometry, beautifully crafted by our academic member,  Maaz Deen Sanjid Kabir.

articles.title: Worm Hole
articles.author: Tawhid Bin Omar
articles.excerpt: Among the most astonishing hypothetical shortcuts in astrophysics, Wormholes challenge our very understanding of cosmic distance. What first appears as an impassable barrier of millions of light-years across the dark void becomes an immediate gateway when spacetime is folded upon itself.

articles.title: Functional Equations
articles.author: Tawhid Bin Omar
articles.excerpt: Among the most profoundly foundational enigmas in algebra, **Functional Equations** invert our traditional understanding of variables to question the very nature of mathematical mappings. What first appears as a chaotic puzzle of unconstrained conditions and elusive expressions becomes beautifully orderly when subjected to the laws of symmetry, injectivity, and substitution. Instead of searching for a hidden number, we hunt for an entire steadfast mathematical identity.

articles.title: Permutations, Combinations and the Art of Counting
articles.author: Tawhid Bin Omar
articles.excerpt: Among the most astonishing hypothetical shortcuts in astrophysics, Wormholes challenge our very understanding of cosmic distance. What first appears as an impassable barrier of millions of light-years across the dark void becomes an immediate gateway when spacetime is folded upon itself.

articles.title: Tensors.....
articles.author: Tawhid Bin Omar
articles.excerpt: Among the most expressive languages in modern mathematics and physics, Tensors reveal the profound geometric truths that remain completely unchanged by our choice of perspective. What first appears as a terrifying maze of multi-dimensional arrays, upper and lower indices, and complex coordinate shifts becomes beautifully simple when viewed as a singular, invariant entity slicing through space and time.

articles.title: Legendre Polynomials and Generating Funstions
articles.author: Tawhid Bin Omar
articles.excerpt: Among the most elegant constructs in mathematical physics, Legendre Polynomials and Generating Functions reveal the underlying symmetry of physical space. What first appears as a chaotic web of complex differential equations and intractable geometric potentials collapses into beautifully ordered orthogonal components when viewed through the lens of a single, masterful generating function. From the gravitational pull of planets to the quantum mechanics of the atom, these steadfast functions transform the geometry of the universe into an orchestra of perfect harmony.

articles.title: Analytic Continuation and the Limits of Generalization
articles.author: Tawhid Bin Omar
articles.excerpt: Among the most revolutionary intellectual achievements in human history, General Relativity unveils the elegant tapestry binding space, time, and gravity. What first appears as a chaotic and mysterious cosmic force acting across empty voids is beautifully unmasked as the simple, dynamic geometry of the universe itself.

articles.title: General Relativity and Space Time
articles.author: Tawhid Bin Omar
articles.excerpt: Among the most revolutionary intellectual achievements in human history, General Relativity unveils the elegant tapestry binding space, time, and gravity. What first appears as a chaotic and mysterious cosmic force acting across empty voids is beautifully unmasked as the simple, dynamic geometry of the universe itself. the article...

articles.title: Jacobian Matrix
articles.author: Tawhid Bin Omar
articles.excerpt: Among the most transformative concepts in multivariable calculus, the Jacobian Matrix reveals the hidden linearity within local chaos. What first appears as a complex, non-linear web of warping coordinates and shifting multidimensional spaces becomes beautifully simple when zoomed in closely along these steadfast local derivatives. It serves as the ultimate mathematical magnifying glass, capturing the precise degree of stretching, rotating, and scaling that occurs when we distort one coordinate system into another.

articles.title: Graph Theory
articles.author: Tawhid Bin Omar
articles.excerpt: Among the most profoundly interconnected fields of mathematics, Graph Theory maps the invisible architecture of relationships. What first appears as a chaotic web of tangled networks, sprawling data points, and isolated entities becomes beautifully simple when stripped down to its core elements: vertices and edges. It reveals that whether we are tracing the neural pathways of the brain, the vast infrastructure of the internet, or the delicate social bonds of humanity, the underlying geometry of connection obeys a steadfast, universal order.

articles.title: Wrap Drive and Faster than Light Travel
articles.author: Tawhid Bin Omar
articles.excerpt: Among the most breathtaking frontiers of theoretical physics is the Warp Drive, anchored by the mathematics of the Alcubierre metric. What first appears as a violation of nature’s absolute speed limit becomes a masterful dance with gravity when viewed through the lens of general relativity. Rather than moving through space faster than light, a warp drive dynamically compresses the fabric of spacetime ahead of a vessel while expanding it behind, allowing humanity to outrun photons by manipulating the geometry of the universe itself.

articles.title: Eigen Vectors
articles.author: Tawhid BIn Omar
articles.excerpt: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors are fundamental concepts in linear algebra used to understand complex matrix transformations. An eigenvector is a special, non-zero vector that does not change direction when a linear transformation is applied. An eigenvalue is simply the scalar factor by which that eigenvector is scaled or stretched.

articles.title: Power of a Point & Radical Axis
articles.author: Tawhid Bin Omar
articles.excerpt: The Power of a Point is a value measuring the relative distance of a point to a circle. The Radical Axis is the straight line containing all points that have the exact same power with respect to two separate circles.

articles.title: Applications of Category Theory in Computer Science and Physics
articles.author: Tawhid Bin Omar
articles.excerpt: Category theory unifies various fields of mathematics by stripping away complex details to reveal underlying structural patterns. The quote perfectly summarizes its power: by standardizing broad concepts, it reframes seemingly difficult, disconnected theorems as intuitive, mechanical consequences

articles.title: The Gamma Function
articles.author: SHARAN HAQUE SAKIN
articles.excerpt: The Gamma Function (denoted by \(\Gamma(z)\)) is a fundamental mathematical tool that extends the concept of the factorial to all real and complex numbers, except for zero and negative integers. For positive integers, it is essentially the factorial of the number minus one.

articles.title: Statistical Physics-Where Worlds Collide
articles.author: Shuvro Anindya Bapari
articles.excerpt: Statistical physics is the bridge between the microscopic world of atoms and the macroscopic world of observable phenomena. By applying probability and statistics, it explains how the collective, randomized behavior of billions of particles directly gives rise to everyday thermodynamic properties like temperature, pressure, and heat.

articles.title: Projective Geometry
articles.author: Tawhid Bin Omar
articles.excerpt: Projective geometry is a branch of mathematics that studies geometric properties which remain unchanged (invariant) under projections, such as perspective or shadows. Unlike Euclidean geometry, it discards measurements like lengths and angles, focusing instead on concepts like collinearity (straight lines) and the intersection of lines.

articles.title: Circles in Coordinate Geometry
articles.author: Tawhid Bin Omar
articles.excerpt: A circle in the coordinate system is the set of all points equidistant from a fixed center point, forming a perfectly round shape. Its size and position are defined by its radius and the coordinates of its center.

articles.title: Straight Lines: Basic to Best
articles.author: Sudipto Sen
articles.excerpt:
A structured and enriched theory document on Straight Lines,
spanning foundational coordinate geometry, engineering-level
problem solving, Olympiad extensions, transformations,
projective geometry, 3D lines, and applications in physics.

interSegments.name: Math Olympiad (Find-based)

interSegments.name: Math Olympiad (Proof-based)

interSegments.description:
Exclusively for Secondary and Higher Secondary categories. 

Duration: 1 Hours 

Format: Proof-based mathematical problems requiring rigorous logical derivations and clear step-by-step proofs.

interSegments.name: IQ Test
interSegments.tagline: Race against the clock in analytical speed reasoning.
interSegments.description:
Open to all categories. 

Format: 20 logic puzzles and pattern-recognition questions designed to test cognitive clarity and analytical depth. 

Duration: 40 Minutes.

interSegments.name: Human Calculator
interSegments.tagline: Unleash super-speed mental arithmetic and calculation loops.
interSegments.description:
Primary & Junior

interSegments.name: Tic-Tac-Toe
interSegments.tagline: Tic-tac-toe is a simple paper-and-pencil game for two players. Players take turns placing an X or an O on a 3x3 grid. The first player to get three of their marks in a row (up, down, across, or diagonal) wins the game.
interSegments.description: Tic-Tac-Toe is a head-to-head, team-based math competition where strategy meets problem-solving. Two teams face off on a standard $3 \times 3$ grid. The objective is to claim three squares in a row—horizontally, vertically, or diagonally—or possess the most claimed squares when time runs out. To mark a cell, the team must successfully answer a primary-level math question assigned to that square before their opponents or within a set time limit.
